issues.description: Attribute naming inconsistency for the same conceptual fields: the problem statement's textual task list names the fields as 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' (problem_statement.md line 17), while the UML in the problem statement and the reference implementation use the longer identifiers 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (problem_statement.md lines 63-69, solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java lines 6-10). This mismatch can confuse students about the exact field names and corresponding getter/setter names they are expected to implement (tests and the provided solution expect the UML-style names), increasing cognitive load and risking failing automated checks that look for the UML-style identifiers.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names consistent across the textual instructions, the UML diagram, the template, and the tests. Recommended action: update the problem statement textual task list to use the UML-style identifiers 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (so the text, UML and reference solution match). Alternatively, if shorter names are preferred, update the UML and solution to 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' and adjust tests accordingly. Ensure examples and getter/setter names in the task text reflect the chosen identifiers.
